summary: Feed s118_double to NDR is degraded: 21.6% of TCP sessions are one-way (exceeds 10% threshold) and 90.7% of bytes are encrypted (exceeds 90% tolerance). No duplicates, drops, overload, or VLAN gaps detected.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker / SPAN is delivering only one direction for ~1 in 5 TCP sessions. Most likely asymmetric routing where RX and TX traverse different links and only one link is tapped, or two SPAN/TAP feeds are not aggregated to the same NDR tool port, so the NDR sees SYN without SYN-ACK/data return.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) to reconstruct TCP state, track sessions, and detect intrusions. With 27/125 sessions one-way, flow reassembly fails, detections are missed, and one-way flows create false positives/noise.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate RX and TX from both sides of asymmetric paths onto the same NDR tool port with flow-aware hashing so each bidirectional session is delivered complete to the NDR.

findings.root_cause: 91% of bytes are TLS/encrypted, just over the NDR's 90% tolerance. Traffic is not being decrypted before the NDR, so payload inspection is blind. This is expected on modern networks but exceeds what this NDR can handle without help.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR needs full payload (needs_full_payload=true) for deep packet inspection and threat detection. With 90.7% encrypted, payload-based detections, JA3, and C2/beacon analysis are severely limited and coverage drops.

recommended_fix.why: NDR cannot inspect encrypted payload natively; add a packet-broker-integrated SSL visibility / decryption zone to selectively decrypt relevant traffic and re-encrypt to tool, or feed decrypted copy to NDR while respecting privacy/policy bypasses.
